children: Malaysia has approved its first spot Bitcoin exchange-traded fund, the Halogen Shariah Bitcoin ETF. The product is scheduled to list on December 2, 2026.
The fund is also set to be the world's first Shariah-compliant spot Bitcoin ETF. It is built for investors who follow Islamic finance principles, though anyone with a brokerage account can buy it.
Halogen Capital Sdn Bhd manages the ETF and is recognized as Malaysia's first licensed digital asset fund manager. Amanie Advisors advises on the fund's Shariah compliance.
The fund is designed to track the FTSE Bitcoin Index. At least 95% of its net asset value (NAV) will sit in spot Bitcoin.
The rest goes into Shariah-compliant liquidity instruments.
Investors get price exposure through a standard brokerage account. They never have to manage a wallet, guard a private key, or worry about losing a seed phrase.
The fund will trade under two tickers. BTCETF-MYR is priced in Malaysian ringgit, and BTCETF-USD is priced in US dollars.
The initial offering can reach up to 1 billion units at an initial NAV of $1 per unit. That could raise around $1 billion, or approximately RM 4.12 billion.
The minimum board lot is 100 units, about $100 at launch.
The annual management fee is up to 0.6% of NAV. The fund plans no income distributions.

The ETF also supports in-kind creations and redemptions in blocks of 50,000 units. Large participants can swap Bitcoin itself for fund units, and the reverse, instead of routing everything through cash.
The fund is aimed at investors with a high risk tolerance and a long investment horizon.
Halogen Capital had assets under management of about RM500 million as of October 31, 2026. A full raise on this ETF would be large next to the manager's existing book.
Halogen already held the country's first license as a digital asset fund manager, and now it is also launching Malaysia's first spot Bitcoin ETF.
The dual-currency setup is a small but useful design choice. Local investors can trade in ringgit, while the USD line lets dollar-based investors skip the currency conversion step.
There are risks. The fund's value will move with Bitcoin, and a Shariah label does nothing to dampen volatility.
Investors buying in for the compliance stamp should understand that it covers how the fund is structured. It says nothing about whether the price goes up.
The 0.6% fee ceiling also deserves attention. Over a long holding period, the yearly fee adds up, and the fund is explicitly targeting long-horizon investors.
The first real test comes on December 2, 2026. Watch how many of the up to 1 billion units actually get taken up, and how closely the market price tracks NAV.

title: Malaysia approves its first spot Bitcoin ETF, and it's Shariah-compliant
